pr_title: core, triedb/pathdb: calculate the size for batch pre-allocation

issue_context.title: The memory preallocated for WriteBatch is always smaller than the actual size in nodebuffer
issue_context.body:
#### System information

Geth version:  1.13
CL client & version: none
OS & Version: Windows/Linux/OSX
Commit hash : master

#### Expected behaviour

https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/b87b9b45331f87fb1da379c5f17a81ebc3738c6e/triedb/pathdb/nodebuffer.go#L209-L236

Pre-allocated memory to avoid re-allocated.

#### Actual behaviour

The calculated size in Nodebuffer is actually slightly smaller than the actual size, which can result in large memory re-allocate(256M+) during the batch.Put process, affecting performance.

#### Steps to reproduce the behaviour

add detailed log to reproduce

```
log.Debug("Persisted pathdb nodes", "nodes", len(b.nodes), "pre-bytes", common.StorageSize(b.size), "bytes", common.StorageSize(size), "elapsed", common.PrettyDuration(time.Since(start)))
```

#### Backtrace

none.
comments: We construct the entire database key as we fulfill the write batch, including the database prefix and the storage owner prefix which are not counted in size. We need to twist the size a bit.

> We construct the entire database key as we fulfill the write batch, including the database prefix and the storage owner prefix which are not counted in size. We need to twist the size a bit.

A simple way to solve the problem that size cannot be calculated precisely is to add a redundancy ratio(5%-10%) to the pre-allocate memory size.

review_comments:
Why don't you calculate it during the `commit`?

https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/8efb094e3541e44e05b04b0bc9f44590080d2b78/triedb/pathdb/nodebuffer.go#L105-L112
IMO it's cleaner to do it as late as possible instead of risking the counters going out of sync with the code. Also less code/fields to keep in mind.
